meta.what_the_collapse_did: Model A of build/SPAN_VS_DAILY_PROPOSAL.md. A row whose condition has no instant at either end -- date_only, whether the ephemeris emitted it as a date or sky.civil_day_span built it, and period_cut -- reprinted one pair of endpoints on every civil day it covered, and the days differed in nothing else. Those are now one row per span carrying first_held and last_held. anchored and named_contacts rows are NOT collapsed, by decision, and neither is any span with a clock time: see row_kinds.row_span in config/conventions.yaml. daily_row_equivalent is what this file would hold under the old shape, so no figure here has to be compared against a number that no longer means what it did.

event_rows.by_tier_note: an event row carries no tier. tier_derivation maps (none, null) to no_rule, so a tier derived here would arrive as 405 more no_rule rows and vanish into the 3,285 verdict rows that already carry it. The sky has no tier.

days.a_day_figure_is_an_overlap_test_since_th: every figure under `days` counts a window row on every civil day it covers, not on its sort date. That is what keeps these three the same numbers they were under the daily render -- 365, 105, 0 and 2 are identical before and after the collapse -- and it is the same overlap rule the HTML date filter applies. See render.covered_days.
days.empty_days_are_output: a day carrying no row is a day on which nothing the astronomy layer tracks happened. Before the base track the calendar could not be empty on any day a rule fired, so it could not report absence at all.
days.why_no_day_is_empty_in_the_unfiltered_vi: days_with_no_row_of_any_kind is 0 and that is NOT because every day carries an event. tier_4 emits a verdict-null USDINR row for every catalogue-B firing, and those blanket all 365 days. So the calendar read whole can never be empty, and the 105 days that carry no astronomical event are visible only through row_kind: filter to row_kind=event and they appear. Absence is reportable on the base track and only through the discriminator.

meta.disclaimer: Financial astrology is a speculative interpretive framework. The dates and conditions in this calendar are computed from an ephemeris and ported from a 2026 source document; the interpretations are that source's claims, carried verbatim or absent. Nothing here is a forecast, a prediction, or investment advice, and no confidence has been raised above `untested` for any row.

Tithi Vriddhi on Pradosh Day: in Bright Fortnight, negativity may not appear; Tithi Kshay on Pradosh Day, in Bright Fortnight, negativity intensifies.

Tithi Vriddhi on Pradosh Day: in Bright Fortnight, negativity may not appear; Tithi Kshay on Pradosh Day, in Bright Fortnight, negativity intensifies.
